        href: "hiphop_periodic_table.html"
      - text: "Codebook"
        href: "data_dictionary.html"
    scrolling: true
    # Below 576px bslib and Quarto stack every row into one column with rows
    # sized to their content; the second rule extends that to tablets, where
    # page 5's four charts sat in 111px columns. A stacked chart takes the
    # widget's 400px default, and once a wrapped title and a legend take their
    # share some plots were under 100px tall, so stacked charts get at least
    # 520px (min-height, so page 3's 900px heatmap keeps its own height).
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        <style>
        @media (max-width: 991.98px) {
          .quarto-dashboard .plotly.html-widget { min-height: 520px; }
        }
        @media (min-width: 576px) and (max-width: 991.98px) {
          .quarto-dashboard .bslib-grid {
            grid-template-columns: 1fr !important;
            grid-template-rows: minmax(1em, max-content) !important;
            height: auto !important;
          }
        }
        </style>
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(scales)
library(forcats)
library(stringr)
library(reactable)
library(htmltools)
library(readxl)

# ── Load data from Excel ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# File lives at: my-site/hiphop/data/hiphop_artists.xlsx
# To add new artists: open the Excel file, append rows to the "Artist Database"
# sheet, then push to main — the publish.yml GitHub Action rebuilds the site.

artists_raw <- read_excel(
  "data/hiphop_artists.xlsx",
  sheet = "Artist Database"
) |>
  # The dataset mixes individual artists ("Element") with groups ("Compound",
  # e.g. Wu-Tang Clan). This dashboard analyses individuals only; groups are
  # shown separately in the periodic table.
  filter(Type == "Element") |>
  rename(
    sym            = Symbol,
    name           = `Artist Name`,
    region         = Region,
    era            = Era,
    style          = Style,
    debut          = `Debut Year`,
    rhyme          = `Rhyme Density`,
    vocab          = `Vocab Breadth`,
    story          = Storytelling,
    metaphor       = `Metaphor/Imagery`,
    concept        = `Conceptual Depth`,
    confidence     = Confidence,
    confidence_note = `Confidence Note`,
    gender         = Gender,
    sig_work       = `Signature Work`,
    active_to      = `Active Through`,
    birth          = `Birth Year`
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(rhyme, vocab, story, metaphor, concept), as.integer))

# ── Derived variables ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
current_year <- as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y"))

artists <- artists_raw |>
  mutate(
    composite = round((rhyme + vocab + story + metaphor + concept) / 5, 1),
    career_end    = coalesce(as.integer(active_to), current_year),
    career_len    = career_end - debut,
    sig_year      = as.integer(str_match(sig_work, "\\((\\d{4})\\)")[, 2]),
    years_to_peak = sig_year - debut,
    age_debut     = debut - birth,
    age_sig       = sig_year - birth,
    era = factor(era, levels = c("Old School","Golden Age","Late 90s","2000s","2010s","2020s")),
    confidence = factor(confidence, levels = c("H","M","L")),
    region = factor(region, levels = c("East Coast","West Coast","South","Midwest")),
    style = factor(style, levels = c(
      "Gangsta/Street", "Trap/Drill", "Political", "Conscious/Lyrical",
      "Abstract", "Experimental", "Jazz-Rap", "Party/Pop"
    )),
    confidence_note = if_else(is.na(confidence_note), "", confidence_note),
    strongest_dim = case_when(
      rhyme == pmax(rhyme, vocab, story, metaphor, concept) ~ "Rhyme Density",
      vocab == pmax(rhyme, vocab, story, metaphor, concept) ~ "Vocab Breadth",
      story == pmax(rhyme, vocab, story, metaphor, concept) ~ "Storytelling",
      metaphor == pmax(rhyme, vocab, story, metaphor, concept) ~ "Metaphor/Imagery",
      TRUE ~ "Conceptual Depth"
    )
  )

# ── Colour palettes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Brand-family categorical hues, borrowed from the periodic table's tile and
# score-bar palettes so the two pages read as one product.
region_pal <- c(
  "East Coast" = "#6f9ec2",
  "West Coast" = "#cf8079",
  "South"      = "#86a866",
  "Midwest"    = "#a085bd"
)

era_pal <- c(
  "Old School" = "#5a9abf",
  "Golden Age" = "#d4b15a",
  "Late 90s"   = "#86a866",
  "2000s"      = "#dd9a5e",
  "2010s"      = "#a085bd",
  "2020s"      = "#cf8079"
)

# Same five hues as the periodic table's modal score bars (SCORE_HUES), so
# each dimension keeps one color across the whole site.
dim_pal <- c(
  "Rhyme Density"    = "#E98973",
  "Vocab Breadth"    = "#8C6A8D",
  "Storytelling"     = "#7aaa8a",
  "Metaphor/Imagery" = "#5a9abf",
  "Conceptual Depth" = "#bf9a40"
)

conf_pal <- c("H" = "#41ab5d", "M" = "#f6c141", "L" = "#e08214")

# Family palette shared with the periodic table (STYLE_COLORS in the template):
# hue = lane, shade = style within it. Corals = the street lane (Gangsta,
# Trap/Drill), jades = the message lane (Political, Conscious/Lyrical),
# purples = the left field (Abstract, Experimental), golds = the crowd lane
# (Jazz-Rap, Party/Pop). CVD-validated 2026-07: worst colorblind pair is
# within-family (13.1, above the strict 12 target), so a confusion is a
# near-miss inside one lane, never a category error. Tooltips still carry
# the style name on every mark.
style_pal <- c(
  "Gangsta/Street"    = "#bd5f50",
  "Trap/Drill"        = "#d98a6d",
  "Political"         = "#008b7e",
  "Conscious/Lyrical" = "#3fbaa0",
  "Abstract"          = "#5f4384",
  "Experimental"      = "#a385c9",
  "Jazz-Rap"          = "#a87d2a",
  "Party/Pop"         = "#d3ab4d"
)

# ── Shared ggplot2 theme ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
theme_hiphop <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_family = "sans", base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", color = "#3C3C3C"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "#555555"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#eeeeee"),
      axis.text     = element_text(color = "#444444"),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title  = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      strip.text    = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#333333")
    )
}

# ── ggplotly() drops ggplot subtitles ────────────────────────────────────────
# Fold each subtitle into the plotly title as a smaller <br><sup> second line
# so it survives the conversion. The <b> wrapper matches the bold title text
# ggplotly emits; the margin bump keeps both lines clear of the plot area.
# Pipe every ggplot chart through this instead of bare ggplotly().
ggplotly_titled <- function(p, ...) {
  fig <- ggplotly(p, ...)
  sub <- p$labels$subtitle
  if (!is.null(sub) && nzchar(sub)) {
    fig <- fig |>
      layout(
        title = list(text = paste0(
          "<b>", p$labels$title, "</b><br><sup>", sub, "</sup>"
        )),
        margin = list(t = 70)
      )
  }
  fit_card(fig)
}

# ── Every chart, ggplot or native plot_ly, ends in fit_card() ────────────────
# The same fixes the two data stories carry, adapted to dashboard cards.
# displayModeBar = FALSE: on a touch screen plotly shows its toolbar all the
# time, and it sat on top of every chart's title.
# fit() wraps the folded title to the chart's width (plotly never wraps a
# title, so on a phone most of them ran off the card, and some did on a
# laptop too) and anchors it to the whole chart rather than the plotting
# area. A dashboard card has a fixed height, so unlike the data stories'
# copy it grows only the top margin: the plot gives up the room, rather
# than the chart growing past the bottom of its card.
# A chart on a page that is not showing draws at plotly's 700px fallback.
# When the page tab is opened, plotly's own responsive handler resizes it
# before a ResizeObserver can see a change, so fit() re-runs after every
# draw instead; it only relayouts when the title or margin actually moves.
# The second hook lays out what sits under the plot: a horizontal legend at the
# chart's bottom edge under the axis title (ggplotly put it a fixed fraction of
# the plot's height below, which landed on the title of a short phone plot), an
# x axis title wrapped when it is wider than the plot, and a y axis title that
# ggplotly drew past the chart's left edge nudged back in. Era labels come in
# on two lines (two_line()); where even that collides, as 2000s, 2010s and
# 2020s do in a plot under about 200px, they tilt on one line instead, and so
# do the heatmaps' one-word dimension names. Below 576px a colour scale is
# hidden: it took most of a phone's width, and each subtitle names the colour.
# A chart drawn at a set height (page 3's heatmap) keeps that height as its
# minimum: below 992px, where cards size from their content, htmlwidgets wrote
# the box 184px shorter than the chart and the 2020s scrolled out of sight.
fit_card <- function(fig) {
  fig |>
    config(responsive = TRUE, displayModeBar = FALSE) |>
    htmlwidgets::onRender("
      function(el) {
        if (el.layout && el.layout.height) el.style.minHeight = el.layout.height + 'px';
        var orig = null, busy = false, canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
        function wrap(text, font, maxW) {
          var ctx = canvas.getContext('2d'), lines = [], line = '';
          ctx.font = font;
          text.split(' ').forEach(function(w) {
            var next = line ? line + ' ' + w : w;
            if (line && ctx.measureText(next).width > maxW) { lines.push(line); line = w; }
            else line = next;
          });
          if (line) lines.push(line);
          return lines;
        }
        function fit() {
          var fl = el._fullLayout;
          if (!fl || !fl.title || !fl.width) return;
          if (orig === null) {
            var m = /^<b>([\\s\\S]*)<\\/b><br><sup>([\\s\\S]*)<\\/sup>$/.exec(fl.title.text || '');
            orig = m ? { title: m[1], sub: m[2], t: fl.margin.t } : false;
          }
          if (!orig) return;
          var size = fl.title.font.size, fam = fl.title.font.family;
          var maxW = fl.width - 16;
          var text =
            wrap(orig.title, 'bold ' + size + 'px ' + fam, maxW)
              .map(function(s) { return '<b>' + s + '</b>'; }).join('<br>') + '<br>' +
            wrap(orig.sub, (size * 0.7) + 'px ' + fam, maxW)
              .map(function(s) { return '<sup>' + s + '</sup>'; }).join('<br>');
          var p = Promise.resolve();
          if (text !== fl.title.text || fl.title.xref !== 'container' || fl.title.x !== 0) {
            p = Plotly.relayout(el, {
              'title.text': text, 'title.xref': 'container', 'title.x': 0,
              'title.xanchor': 'left', 'title.pad.l': 8,
              'title.yref': 'container', 'title.y': 1, 'title.yanchor': 'top'
            });
          }
          p.then(function() {
            var g = el.querySelector('.gtitle');
            if (!g) return;
            var box = g.getBoundingClientRect(), top = el.getBoundingClientRect().top;
            var padT = Math.max(0, (el._fullLayout.title.pad.t || 0) + 8 - (box.top - top));
            var need = Math.max(orig.t, Math.ceil(padT + box.height) + 20);
            if (Math.abs(need - el._fullLayout.margin.t) > 2) {
              Plotly.relayout(el, { 'margin.t': need, 'title.pad.t': padT });
            }
          });
        }
        fit();
        el.on('plotly_afterplot', function() {
          if (busy) return;
          busy = true;
          setTimeout(function() { busy = false; fit(); }, 0);
        });
      }
    ") |>
    htmlwidgets::onRender("
      function(el) {
        // Everything under or beside the plotting area, laid out in pixels
        // after each draw: an x axis title wider than the plot wraps, a
        // horizontal legend sits at the bottom of the chart under the axis
        // title (ggplotly sets it a fixed fraction of the plot's height
        // below, which on a short phone plot lands on the title), and a y
        // axis title drawn past the chart's left edge is nudged back in.
        var busy = false, xt = null, ticks = null, canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
        function below() {
          var fl = el._fullLayout;
          if (!fl || !fl.width || !fl.xaxis) return;
          var box = el.getBoundingClientRect(), ups = {};
          if (xt === null) xt = (fl.xaxis.title && fl.xaxis.title.text) || '';
          if (xt && xt.indexOf('<br>') < 0) {
            var f = fl.xaxis.title.font, ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
            ctx.font = f.size + 'px ' + f.family;
            var words = xt.split(' '), text = xt;
            if (words.length > 1 && ctx.measureText(xt).width > fl._size.w) {
              var half = Math.ceil(words.length / 2);
              text = words.slice(0, half).join(' ') + '<br>' + words.slice(half).join(' ');
            }
            if (text !== fl.xaxis.title.text) ups['xaxis.title.text'] = text;
          }
          // Word labels on an x axis (eras, set on two lines; the heatmaps'
          // dimension names) tilt onto one line wherever the widest line is
          // wider than its share of the plot, as 2000s and 2010s are in a plot
          // under about 200px. Numeric axes never tilt.
          var xa = fl.xaxis;
          if (ticks === null) {
            ticks = (xa.ticktext || []).some(function(t) { return isNaN(parseFloat(t)); })
              ? xa.ticktext.slice() : false;
          }
          if (ticks) {
            var c2 = canvas.getContext('2d'), widest = 0;
            c2.font = xa.tickfont.size + 'px ' + xa.tickfont.family;
            ticks.forEach(function(t) {
              t.split(/<br\\s*\\/?>/).forEach(function(s) { widest = Math.max(widest, c2.measureText(s).width); });
            });
            var tilt = widest + 6 > fl._size.w / ticks.length;
            var want = tilt ? ticks.map(function(t) { return t.replace(/<br\\s*\\/?>/g, ' '); }) : ticks;
            if (want.join('|') !== xa.ticktext.join('|') || (tilt ? -45 : 0) !== (xa.tickangle || 0)) {
              ups['xaxis.ticktext'] = want; ups['xaxis.tickangle'] = tilt ? -45 : 0;
            }
          }
          // On a phone a colour scale took most of the chart's width (the
          // canon map and fingerprints kept a 64px plot), so below 576px it is
          // hidden: each chart's subtitle says what the colour means and a tap
          // on any mark gives its value.
          for (var i = 0; i < el.data.length; i++) {
            var m = el.data[i].marker;
            if (!m || !m.colorbar) continue;
            var show = window.innerWidth >= 576;
            if ((m.showscale !== false) !== show) { Plotly.restyle(el, { 'marker.showscale': show }, [i]); return; }
          }
          if (fl.showlegend && fl.legend.orientation === 'h' && fl.legend.yref !== 'container') {
            ups['legend.x'] = 0; ups['legend.xanchor'] = 'left';
            ups['legend.yref'] = 'container'; ups['legend.y'] = 0;
            ups['legend.yanchor'] = 'bottom';
          }
          if (Object.keys(ups).length) { Plotly.relayout(el, ups); return; }
          var plotBottom = fl.height - fl.margin.b, low = plotBottom, left = box.left;
          el.querySelectorAll('.xtick text, .g-xtitle text, .xtitle').forEach(function(t) {
            var r = t.getBoundingClientRect();
            if (r.height) low = Math.max(low, r.bottom - box.top);
          });
          el.querySelectorAll('.ytitle, .annotation-text').forEach(function(t) {
            var r = t.getBoundingClientRect();
            if (r.width) left = Math.min(left, r.left);
          });
          if (left < box.left - 0.5) ups['margin.l'] = fl.margin.l + Math.ceil(box.left - left) + 4;
          var lg = fl.showlegend && fl.legend.orientation === 'h' && el.querySelector('.legend');
          if (lg) {
            var need = Math.ceil(low - plotBottom) + Math.ceil(lg.getBoundingClientRect().height) + 12;
            if (Math.abs(need - fl.margin.b) > 2) ups['margin.b'] = need;
          }
          if (Object.keys(ups).length) Plotly.relayout(el, ups);
        }
        below();
        el.on('plotly_afterplot', function() {
          if (busy) return;
          busy = true;
          setTimeout(function() { busy = false; below(); }, 30);
        });
      }
    ")
}

# Era names on an x axis break at their space ("Old School" over two lines),
# which fit_card() tilts back onto one line only where a plot is too narrow.
two_line <- function(x) sub(" ", "\n", x, fixed = TRUE)
```

# Overview {.sidebar}

```{r sidebar-summary}
n_artists  <- nrow(artists)
n_high     <- sum(artists$confidence == "H")
n_medium   <- sum(artists$confidence == "M")
n_low      <- sum(artists$confidence == "L")
avg_comp   <- round(mean(artists$composite), 2)
top_artist <- artists |> slice_max(composite, n = 1) |> pull(name)

tagList(
  tags$div(style = "padding: 1rem 0;",
    tags$h4("Dataset at a Glance", style = "color:#3C3C3C; font-weight:700;"),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color:#dddddd;"),
    tags$p(tags$strong(n_artists), " artists across 6 eras"),
    tags$p(tags$strong(length(levels(artists$region))), " geographic regions"),
    tags$p(tags$strong(length(levels(artists$style))), " lyrical styles"),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color:#dddddd;"),
    tags$h5("Confidence breakdown", style = "color:#555;"),
    tags$p(
      tags$span(style = "color:#41ab5d; font-weight:700;", paste0("H: ", n_high, " artists")),
      tags$br(),
      tags$span(style = "color:#c8a000; font-weight:700;", paste0("M: ", n_medium, " artists (some gaps)")),
      tags$br(),
      tags$span(style = "color:#e08214; font-weight:700;", paste0("L: ", n_low, " artists (estimates only)"))
    ),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color:#dddddd;"),
    tags$h5("Mean composite score", style = "color:#555;"),
    tags$p(tags$strong(avg_comp, " / 10")),
    tags$p(tags$em(paste0("Highest: ", top_artist))),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color:#dddddd;"),
    tags$h5("Teaching concepts", style = "color:#555; margin-top:1rem;"),
    tags$ul(style = "padding-left:1.2rem; font-size:0.85rem;",
      tags$li("Measurement validity"),
      tags$li("Sampling & bias"),
      tags$li("Multidimensional scoring"),
      tags$li("Composite vs. dimensions"),
      tags$li("Uncertainty communication"),
      tags$li("Visualization design")
    )
  )
)
```

# 1 · What Are We Measuring?

## Row {height="15%"}

::: {.callout-tip title="Teaching Prompt: Construct Validity"}
**The central measurement problem:** We started with one variable called "Lyricism" and ended up with five. Was that the right decision? What are we gaining and losing? This is the construct validity question that underlies every performance measure, survey instrument, and rating scale in your organization.
:::

## Row {height="85%"}

### Radar: One Artist, Five Dimensions {width="40%"}

```{r radar-single}
radar_artists <- c("Kendrick Lamar", "Scarface", "MF DOOM", "Rakim")

radar_data <- artists |>
  filter(name %in% radar_artists) |>
  select(name, rhyme, vocab, story, metaphor, concept) |>
  pivot_longer(-name, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "score") |>
  mutate(dimension = recode(dimension,
    rhyme    = "Rhyme Density",
    vocab    = "Vocab Breadth",
    story    = "Storytelling",
    metaphor = "Metaphor/Imagery",
    concept  = "Conceptual Depth"
  ))

fig_radar <- plot_ly(type = "scatterpolar", fill = "toself", mode = "lines+markers")

colors_radar <- c("#8C6A8D","#E98973","#5a9abf","#bf9a40")
for (i in seq_along(radar_artists)) {
  d <- radar_data |> filter(name == radar_artists[i])
  fig_radar <- fig_radar |> add_trace(
    r = c(d$score, d$score[1]),
    theta = c(d$dimension, d$dimension[1]),
    name = radar_artists[i],
    line = list(color = colors_radar[i], width = 2),
    fillcolor = paste0(colors_radar[i], "22")
  )
}

fig_radar |>
  layout(
    polar = list(radialaxis = list(visible = TRUE, range = c(0, 10), tickfont = list(size = 10))),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0.1, y = -0.1),
    margin = list(t = 10, b = 10),
    paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    plot_bgcolor  = "rgba(0,0,0,0)"
  ) |>
  fit_card()
```

### Scatter: Composite Score vs. Storytelling {width="60%"}

```{r scatter-composite-v-story}
p_scatter <- artists |>
  filter(confidence != "L") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = story, y = composite,
             color = era, size = composite,
             text = paste0(
               "<b>", name, "</b><br>",
               "Era: ", era, "<br>",
               "Composite: ", composite, "<br>",
               "Storytelling: ", story, "<br>",
               "Rhyme Density: ", rhyme
             ))) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.75, width = 0.15, height = 0.05) +
  scale_color_manual(values = era_pal) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 6), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(2, 10.5), breaks = seq(2, 10, 2)) +
  labs(
    title = "Composite score vs. Storytelling dimension",
    subtitle = "Artists with the same composite can have very different dimension profiles",
    x = "Storytelling score (1–10)",
    y = "Composite score",
    color = "Era"
  ) +
  theme_hiphop() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggplotly_titled(p_scatter, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(
    paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    plot_bgcolor  = "rgba(0,0,0,0)"
  )
```

# 2 · Who Is In the Data?

## Row {height="15%"}

::: {.callout-warning title="Teaching Prompt: Sampling Decisions and Bias"}
**Every dataset has a frame, and every frame has a gap.** This dataset over-represents critically acclaimed artists, the East Coast (NYC especially), the Golden Age, and men. Those are documented choices. What datasets do you use at work where nobody wrote the frame down? Who is missing?
:::

## Row {height="45%"}

### Artists by Region {width="50%"}

```{r bar-region}
p_region <- artists |>
  count(region, era) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_rev(region), y = n, fill = era,
             text = paste0(era, ": ", n, " artists"))) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = era_pal) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Artists by region and era",
    subtitle = "The East Coast and South dominate; international scenes sit outside the frame",
    x = NULL, y = "Number of artists", fill = "Era"
  ) +
  theme_hiphop()

ggplotly_titled(p_region, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")
```

### Gender Representation Gap {width="50%"}

```{r bar-gender}
# Gender comes from the Gender column in the Excel workbook (single source of
# truth). "Mixed" only occurs for Compounds, which this dashboard filters out.
gender_data <- artists |>
  count(era, gender_group = gender)

n_female <- sum(artists$gender == "Female")

p_gender <- gender_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = era, y = n, fill = gender_group,
             text = paste0(gender_group, ": ", n, " artists"))) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Female" = "#c180a2", "Male" = "#b3abb3")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Gender representation by era",
    subtitle = paste0(
      n_female, " female artists of ", nrow(artists), " total (",
      round(n_female/nrow(artists)*100), "%)"
    ),
    x = NULL, y = "Share of era", fill = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = two_line) +
  theme_hiphop()

ggplotly_titled(p_gender, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")
```

### What Bias Looks Like in Practice {width="65%"}

```{r bias-table}
bias_df <- tribble(
  ~"Bias type",        ~"Direction",                              ~"Practical implication",
  "Prestige",         "Over-represents critically acclaimed artists", "Commercial artists scored lower; vibe-first artists may be underrated",
  "Gender",           "~22% female vs. ~50% of rap audience",    "Female artists face different critical frameworks; scores may not be comparable",
  "Geography",        "East Coast + Golden Age disproportionate", "Southern and international artists underrepresented in critical canon used for scoring",
  "Language",         "English-language, US-based frame only",    "International and non-English rap is excluded from the sampling frame entirely, a documented scope decision rather than an oversight",
  "Survivorship",     "Only artists who entered critical canon",  "Regionally significant artists without national coverage are absent",
  "Recency (inverted)","Post-2020 artists scored conservatively", "Emerging talent may be systematically underscored; revisit annually"
)

reactable(
  bias_df,
  columns = list(
    "Bias type"             = colDef(minWidth = 100, style = list(fontWeight = "600")),
    "Direction"             = colDef(minWidth = 160),
    "Practical implication" = colDef(minWidth = 200)
  ),
  striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE, bordered = TRUE,
  theme = reactableTheme(
    headerStyle = list(background = "#2E1A47", color = "#ffffff", fontWeight = "600")
  )
)
```

# 3 · Dimensions vs. Composite

## Row {height="15%"}

::: {.callout-note title="Teaching Prompt: The Averaging Problem"}
**What does averaging destroy?** Rakim (Rhyme Density 10, composite 8.8) and Scarface (Storytelling 10, composite 8.2) sit six tenths of a point apart on the composite, yet their profiles look nothing alike. Does that similarity mean anything, or does the average erase the most important information? When does averaging help, and when does it mislead?
:::

## Row {height="1260px"}

### Heatmap: All Artists, All Dimensions

```{r heatmap-dims}
# One panel, not facet_grid(era ~ .): ggplotly ignores space = "free_y", so
# every era got the same height and the 2010s' 23 artists overprinted while
# Old School's 4 sat in 25px rows, and the era strips on the right were cut
# off on a phone. Each era now opens with a bold heading row in the name
# column, every artist row is the same height, and the chart is sized to its
# rows. Artists run highest composite first within an era, as before.
heat_artists <- artists |>
  filter(confidence == "H") |>
  arrange(era, desc(composite)) |>
  select(name, era, rhyme, vocab, story, metaphor, concept)

heat_rows <- unlist(lapply(levels(droplevels(heat_artists$era)), function(e) {
  c(paste0("era: ", e), heat_artists$name[heat_artists$era == e])
}))
heat_h <- length(heat_rows) * 14 + 160
# Page 3's rows are fixed heights because its grid sizes from content, and
# the percentage row this chart shared capped it at 797px, cropping the 2020s
# and the dimension names. Its row is 1260px, so a taller chart would be
# cropped again: when the guard fails, raise that row with the data.
stopifnot(heat_h <= 1220)

dim_long <- heat_artists |>
  pivot_longer(rhyme:concept, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "score") |>
  mutate(
    dimension = recode(dimension,
      rhyme    = "Rhyme",
      vocab    = "Vocab",
      story    = "Story",
      metaphor = "Metaphor",
      concept  = "Concept"
    ),
    dimension = factor(dimension, levels = c("Rhyme","Vocab","Story","Metaphor","Concept"))
  )

p_heat <- dim_long |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dimension, y = name, fill = score,
             text = paste0(name, " · ", dimension, ": ", score))) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#f6f0f6", mid = "#a87ea9", high = "#4a2d4b",
    midpoint = 5.5, limits = c(1, 10),
    name = "Score"
  ) +
  # heading rows have no tiles; limits keeps them as empty rows in order
  scale_y_discrete(
    limits = rev(heat_rows),
    labels = function(x) ifelse(startsWith(x, "era: "),
                                paste0("<b>", sub("era: ", "", x, fixed = TRUE), "</b>"), x)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Dimension scores by artist (High-confidence only)",
    subtitle = "Each column is a dimension; each row an artist; color = score 1–10",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_hiphop() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.25),  # 11px, the site's floor
    panel.grid.major = element_blank()
  )

ggplotly_titled(p_heat, tooltip = "text", height = heat_h) |>
  # dimension names across the top, where a tall chart cannot crop them
  layout(xaxis = list(side = "top"),
         paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")
```

## Row {height="520px"}

# 4 · Uncertainty in Practice

## Row {height="15%"}

::: {.callout-important title="Teaching Prompt: Communicating Uncertainty"}
**Most dashboards show you the number. This one shows you how much to trust it.** The confidence flag almost never shows up in stakeholder reporting, but it should. Where in your organization's reporting does uncertainty get hidden? What decisions are being made on L-confidence data presented as H-confidence?
:::

## Row {height="45%"}

### Composite Distribution by Confidence Tier {width="50%"}

```{r violin-confidence}
violin_data <- artists |>
  mutate(
    conf_label = factor(
      case_when(confidence == "H" ~ "High", confidence == "M" ~ "Medium", TRUE ~ "Low"),
      levels = c("High", "Medium", "Low")
    ),
    composite = as.numeric(composite)
  )

plot_ly(
  violin_data,
  x        = ~conf_label,
  y        = ~composite,
  split    = ~conf_label,
  type     = "violin",
  text     = ~paste0(name, ": ", composite),
  hoverinfo = "text",
  points   = "all",
  jitter   = 0.3,
  pointpos = 0,
  opacity  = 0.6,
  marker   = list(size = 5, opacity = 0.8),
  color    = ~conf_label,
  colors   = c("High" = "#41ab5d", "Medium" = "#f6c141", "Low" = "#e08214"),
  showlegend = FALSE
) |>
  layout(
    title  = list(text = "Score distribution by confidence tier",
                  font = list(size = 14, color = "#3C3C3C")),
    xaxis  = list(title = "Confidence tier"),
    yaxis  = list(title = "Composite score", range = c(1, 10.5)),
    paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    plot_bgcolor  = "rgba(0,0,0,0)"
  ) |>
  fit_card()
```

### Score Range: What We Don't Know {width="50%"}

```{r uncertainty-range}
uncertain <- artists |>
  filter(confidence %in% c("M","L")) |>
  arrange(desc(composite)) |>
  head(25) |>
  mutate(
    lo = pmax(1,  composite - if_else(confidence == "M", 0.8, 1.6)),
    hi = pmin(10, composite + if_else(confidence == "M", 0.8, 1.6)),
    name = fct_reorder(name, composite)
  )

p_range <- uncertain |>
  ggplot(aes(y = name, color = confidence,
             text = paste0(name, "\nScore: ", composite,
                           "\nPlausible range: ", round(lo,1), "–", round(hi,1)))) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = lo, xend = hi, yend = name), linewidth = 1.8, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(x = composite), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = conf_pal,
                     labels = c("M" = "Medium (±0.8)", "L" = "Low (±1.6)")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1, 10), breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(
    title = "Plausible score ranges for less-documented artists",
    subtitle = "Point = scored value; bar = plausible range given evidence quality",
    x = "Composite score", y = NULL, color = "Confidence tier"
  ) +
  theme_hiphop()

ggplotly_titled(p_range, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")
```

# 5 · Visualization Design

## Row {height="15%"}

::: {.callout-tip title="Teaching Prompt: The Same Data, Different Stories"}
**Every visualization choice is an argument.** The four charts below show the same data (composite scores by era) drawn four different ways. Each one highlights something and hides something else. Which is most honest? Which is most persuasive? Are those the same chart?
:::

## Row {height="85%"}

### A: Ranked Bar {width="25%"}

```{r viz-bar}

  group_by(era) |>
  summarise(mean_comp = round(mean(composite), 2), .groups = "drop")

p_bar <- era_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(era, mean_comp), y = mean_comp, fill = era,
             text = paste0(era, ": ", mean_comp))) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = era_pal) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 10), breaks = c(0, 5, 10)) +
  labs(title = "A: Bar chart", subtitle = "Ranking emphasis", x = NULL, y = "Mean composite") +
  theme_hiphop()

ggplotly_titled(p_bar, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")
```

```{r viz-line}

             text = paste0(era, ": ", mean_comp))) +
  geom_line(color = "#444444", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = era_pal) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(5.5, 8.5)) +

ggplotly_titled(p_line, tooltip = "text") |>
```

### C: Distribution (Violin) {width="25%"}

```{r viz-violin}
era_levels <- levels(artists$era)

plot_ly(
  artists |> mutate(composite = as.numeric(composite)),
  x        = ~era,
  y        = ~composite,

    title  = list(text = "<b>C: Violin + box</b><br><sup>Distribution emphasis</sup>",
```

# 6 · One More Variable

## Row

::: {.callout-tip title="Teaching Prompt: The Cost of a Channel"}
**Every encoding channel is a tax on the reader.** Position, color, panels, size: each added variable buys information and costs attention. The first four charts ask one question (do vocabulary and rhyme craft travel together?) and add one variable at a time. Somewhere along the way the chart stops earning its ink. Decide where, then look at the last two charts, which spend the same budget differently. One scope note: Jazz-Rap does not appear on this page, because all four Jazz-Rap acts are groups and this dashboard charts solo acts.
:::

## Row

### 1 · Two Variables {width="50%"}

```{r ladder-two}
r_vr <- cor(artists$vocab, artists$rhyme)

  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(2, 10, 2)) +
  labs(
    title = "1: Position only",
    subtitle = paste0("Vocab vs rhyme across ", nrow(artists),
                      " solo acts, r = ", sprintf("%.2f", r_vr),
                      ". One skill or two?"),
    x = "Rhyme Density (1–10)", y = "Vocab Breadth (1–10)"
  ) +
  theme_hiphop()

ggplotly_titled(p_two, tooltip = "text") |>
```


## Row

### The Canon Map {width="50%"}

```{r canon-map}
style_order <- artists |>
  count(style, sort = TRUE) |>
  pull(style) |>
  as.character()

canon <- artists |>
  group_by(era, style) |>
  summarise(n_acts = n(), mean_comp = round(mean(composite), 1),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(style = factor(as.character(style), levels = rev(style_order)))

p_canon <- canon |>
  ggplot(aes(x = era, y = style,
             text = paste0(style, " · ", era, "<br>", n_acts,
                           " acts · mean composite ", mean_comp))) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_acts, color = mean_comp), alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 13, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#e7dbe7", high = "#4a2d4b",
                       name = "Mean composite") +
  labs(
    title = "The canon map: four variables, spent well",
    subtitle = "Size = number of solo acts; color = mean composite. Style and era ride on position, so no channel is overloaded",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = two_line) +
  theme_hiphop() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#f0eaf0"))

ggplotly_titled(p_canon, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")
```

### Style Fingerprints {width="50%"}

```{r style-fingerprints}
fingerprints <- artists |>
  select(style, Rhyme = rhyme, Vocab = vocab, Story = story,
         Metaphor = metaphor, Concept = concept) |>
  pivot_longer(-style, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "score") |>
  group_by(dimension) |>
  mutate(dim_mean = mean(score)) |>
  group_by(style, dimension, dim_mean) |>
  summarise(avg = mean(score), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    dev = avg - dim_mean,
    dimension = factor(dimension,
                       levels = c("Rhyme", "Vocab", "Story", "Metaphor", "Concept")),
    style = factor(as.character(style), levels = rev(style_order))
  )

p_finger <- fingerprints |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dimension, y = style, fill = dev,
             text = paste0(style, " · ", dimension, "<br>mean ", round(avg, 1),
                           " (", ifelse(dev >= 0, "+", ""), round(dev, 1),
                           " vs all solo acts)"))) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#33607f", mid = "#f2f0ee", high = "#b05a42",
                       midpoint = 0, name = "vs overall mean") +
  labs(
    title = "Style fingerprints: three variables, falsifiable",
    subtitle = "Warm = above the all-acts mean on that dimension, cool = below. Every taxonomy definition is checkable here",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_hiphop()

ggplotly_titled(p_finger, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")
```

# 7 · Careers & Longevity

## Row {height="15%"}

::: {.callout-warning title="Teaching Prompt: Survivorship & the Canon"}
**Does the composite measure quality, or career length?** Critical writing accumulates over a career: the longer an act stays active, the more analyses exist to score them with. Watch how scores drift upward with career length, then ask which way the causality runs. And notice how quickly most acts produce their signature work. If the defining album usually lands within a few years of debut, what exactly is a thirty-year career adding to the number? Age cuts the same question a different way: if the defining work reliably arrives in an artist's mid-twenties, era after era, what does that say about how the genre treats its elders?
:::

## Row {height="42.5%"}

### Career Length vs. Composite {width="55%"}

```{r career-scatter}
career_data <- artists |>
  mutate(
    status = if_else(is.na(active_to), "Active", "Concluded"),
    span_label = paste0(debut, "–", if_else(is.na(active_to), "present", as.character(active_to)))
  )

p_career <- career_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = career_len, y = composite, color = era,
             text = paste0(
               "<b>", name, "</b><br>",
               "Active: ", span_label, " (", career_len, " yrs, ", status, ")<br>",
               "Signature: ", if_else(is.na(sig_work), "none recorded", sig_work), "<br>",
               "Composite: ", composite
             ))) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0.05, alpha = 0.75, size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = era_pal) +
  labs(
    title = "Career length vs. composite score",
    subtitle = "Length = debut through last active year (or present). Does longevity buy critical standing?",
    x = "Career length (years)", y = "Composite score", color = "Era"
  ) +
  theme_hiphop() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggplotly_titled(p_career, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")
```

### Years from Debut to Signature Work {width="45%"}

```{r years-to-peak}
peak_data   <- artists |> filter(!is.na(years_to_peak))
med_peak    <- median(peak_data$years_to_peak)
peak_counts <- peak_data |> count(years_to_peak)

p_peak <- peak_counts |>
  ggplot(aes(x = years_to_peak, y = n,
             text = paste0(years_to_peak, " yrs after debut: ", n, " acts"))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#6f9ec2", color = "white", linewidth = 0.3, width = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = med_peak, linetype = "dashed", color = "#cf8079", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = med_peak + 0.5, y = max(peak_counts$n) * 0.95, hjust = 0,
           label = paste0("median: ", med_peak, " yrs"), color = "#cf8079", size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "How fast does the defining work arrive?",
    subtitle = "Years from debut to consensus signature release",
    x = "Years from debut to signature work", y = "Number of acts"
  ) +
  theme_hiphop()

ggplotly_titled(p_peak, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")
```

## Row {height="42.5%"}

### Age at Debut, by Era {width="50%"}

```{r age-debut-era}
# Solo artists only: Compounds carry no Birth Year (members vary in age).
age_data <- artists |> filter(!is.na(birth))

p_age_debut <- age_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = era, y = age_debut)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(group = era), fill = "#d4b15a", alpha = 0.35,
               color = "#7a6a7b", outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = era,
                  text = paste0("<b>", name, "</b><br>",
                                "Born ", birth, ", debut ", debut,
                                " at age ", age_debut)),
              width = 0.18, height = 0.1, alpha = 0.75, size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = era_pal, guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Age at debut, by era",
    subtitle = "Is the genre debuting younger over time?",
    x = NULL, y = "Age at first commercial release"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = two_line) +
  theme_hiphop()

ggplotly_titled(p_age_debut, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")
```

### Age at Signature Work vs. Composite {width="50%"}

```{r age-sig-composite}
sig_age_data <- age_data |> filter(!is.na(age_sig))
med_age_sig  <- median(sig_age_data$age_sig)

p_age_sig <- sig_age_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age_sig, y = composite, color = era,
             text = paste0("<b>", name, "</b><br>",
                           "Signature: ", sig_work, " at age ", age_sig, "<br>",
                           "Composite: ", composite))) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0.05, alpha = 0.75, size = 2.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = med_age_sig, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "#7a6a7b", linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = era_pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(15, 45, 5)) +
  labs(
    title = "Age at signature work vs. composite",
    subtitle = paste0("Do prodigies score higher? Median signature-work age: ",
                      med_age_sig),
    x = "Age when the signature work landed", y = "Composite score", color = "Era"
  ) +
  theme_hiphop() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggplotly_titled(p_age_sig, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")
```

# 8 · Full Data Table

## Row

```{r full-table}
display_data <- artists |>
  select(
    Symbol = sym, Artist = name, Region = region, Era = era, Style = style,
    Debut = debut, Rhyme = rhyme, Vocab = vocab, Story = story,
    Metaphor = metaphor, Concept = concept, Composite = composite,
    Conf = confidence
  ) |>
  arrange(Era, desc(Composite))

reactable(
  display_data,
  columns = list(
    Symbol    = colDef(maxWidth = 65, style = list(fontWeight = "700", color = "#2E1A47")),
    Artist    = colDef(minWidth = 150, style = list(fontWeight = "600")),
    Region    = colDef(maxWidth = 110),
    Era       = colDef(maxWidth = 110),
    Style     = colDef(minWidth = 145),
    Debut     = colDef(maxWidth = 70),
    Rhyme     = colDef(maxWidth = 65,
      style = function(v) list(background = colorRampPalette(c("#fdf0ec","#b05a42"))(10)[max(1,v)],
                                color = if(v >= 7) "#fff" else "#000")),
    Vocab     = colDef(maxWidth = 65,
      style = function(v) list(background = colorRampPalette(c("#f3edf3","#5d4360"))(10)[max(1,v)],
                                color = if(v >= 7) "#fff" else "#000")),
    Story     = colDef(maxWidth = 65,
      style = function(v) list(background = colorRampPalette(c("#edf4ef","#3f6b50"))(10)[max(1,v)],
                                color = if(v >= 7) "#fff" else "#000")),
    Metaphor  = colDef(maxWidth = 75,
      style = function(v) list(background = colorRampPalette(c("#ecf3f8","#33607f"))(10)[max(1,v)],
                                color = if(v >= 7) "#fff" else "#000")),
    Concept   = colDef(maxWidth = 75,
      style = function(v) list(background = colorRampPalette(c("#f8f3e4","#7a5f22"))(10)[max(1,v)],
                                color = if(v >= 7) "#fff" else "#000")),
    Composite = colDef(maxWidth = 85, style = list(fontWeight = "700", background = "#2E1A47", color = "#fff")),
    Conf      = colDef(maxWidth = 55,
      style = function(v) {
        color <- switch(v, H = "#41ab5d", M = "#c8a000", L = "#e08214", "#000")
        list(fontWeight = "700", color = color)
      })
  ),
  searchable = TRUE, filterable = TRUE, sortable = TRUE,
  striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE, bordered = TRUE,
  defaultPageSize = 25, showPageSizeOptions = TRUE,
  theme = reactableTheme(
    headerStyle = list(background = "#2E1A47", color = "#ffffff", fontWeight = "600")
  )
)
```
